column1: # JOACHIM PETER LEIBHOLZ DIED AT TOORAK IN 1971, AND THE INDEX NAMES HIS PARENTS.
# Registry of Births Deaths and Marriages Victoria, historical index, searched 21 September 2026.

column2: LEIBHOLZ · Joachim Peter · Death · Mother's name NANETTE · Mother's family name at birth NETTER · Father's name LEIBHOLZ WILLIAM · Place of birth BERLIN GERMANY · Place of death TOORAK · Age at Death 68 · Reg. year 1971 · Reg. number 26252/1971.

HE STAYED. The NAA had him landing at Melbourne from the ANCHISES on 12 June 1939 and naturalised at South Yarra in 1944, and nothing after that. He died thirty-two years later at TOORAK, two suburbs from where he naturalised, aged 68 — consistent to the year with a birth on 20 August 1903.

column1: *** AND IT GIVES HIM PARENTS, WHICH IS THE POINT ***
column2: WILLIAM LEIBHOLZ and NANETTE née NETTER. Neither name has ever been in this archive attached to him.

column1: *** AND THIS ARCHIVE HAS ALREADY MET A WILLIAM LEIBHOLZ OF BERLIN ***
column2: the Berliner Adressbuch work records, for 1920, "WILLIAM LEIBHOLZ, GENERALDIREKTOR and STADTRAT — a city councillor", and the 1913 name section read on 20 September gives "William, Kaufm., W15, Kurfürstendamm 169". A managing director and city councillor on the Kurfürstendamm.

THE IDENTIFICATION IS STRONG AND IS NOT PROOF. William was not a common forename among Berlin Leibholz men — the 1913 roll lists exactly one — and a Berlin-born son of a William Leibholz who reaches Melbourne in 1939 is the shape of that household. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT is the death certificate itself, which Victoria sells and which carries the parents in full, or a Berlin record naming William's wife as Nanette Netter.

column1: and what it does NOT do
column2: CONNECT HIM TO THIS FAMILY. Our Leibholzes are Konfektion merchants from Schubin; William is a Generaldirektor on the Kurfürstendamm. Nothing joins them but the surname, and the surname is the thing these three days have shown to be unreliable in both directions. THE MELBOURNE LANE STAYS A LANE.

the Victorian index accepts a wildcard, so the search was run as *** L*HOLZ *** across BIRTHS, DEATHS AND MARRIAGES, 1900 to 1995. It returns EXACTLY THIS ONE RECORD. No Leipholz, no Laibholz, no Leibholtz, and no second Leibholz of any kind in the whole of Victoria.

column1: and the limit of that negative, which matters
column2: the Victorian historical indexes close at different dates by event — births around 1922, marriages around 1942, deaths around 1988. SO THE CHILD WHO CAME OFF THE ANCHISES IN 1939 WOULD NOT APPEAR AS A VICTORIAN BIRTH whatever happened, and a marriage after 1942 would not appear either. The negative is about the index's window, not about the family.

the child. NAA MP56/10 catalogues "LEIBHOLZ Tilde [AND CHILD] — arrived Melbourne per Anchises 12 June 1939" and does not name them. That file is at the NAA's Melbourne office and is in the access-examination letter.
